answer: Treat peer attestations as a graph and let random walks decide pay. Each epoch, run 2,000 ten-hop walks from 20 long-audited seed agents; an ID's reward is capped by how many walks end on it. An honest garden of agents is densely cross-attested, so walks spread through it. A sybil farm can mint 100 IDs, but it reaches honest agents only through the few attestations it truly earned, so every walk entering it squeezes through those edges and 100 clones split what a handful of real IDs would get. No gale of signups redraws the atlas of real trust edges. Numbers are illustrative.
